evals.prompt: I'm writing the main per-frame render loop for a low-level explicit-API renderer (Vulkan-style). Each frame I record command buffers and update a uniform buffer with camera and per-object data, then submit and present. How should I structure the loop and its resources so the CPU can prepare the next frame while the GPU works on the current one, without corrupting data the GPU is still reading?
assertions: At the start of a frame, waits on the fence for the frame slot it is about to reuse (e.g. frame index modulo N), NOT the fence of the frame just submitted
Keeps only about 2 or 3 frames in flight (double/triple buffering) rather than maximizing the number of in-flight frames
Duplicates per-frame CPU-written GPU resources (uniform/command/instance buffers) per frame slot so writing one slot cannot race the GPU reading another

evals.prompt: I'm building a renderer with a deferred pipeline: a G-buffer pass, an SSAO pass, a lighting pass, and a bloom mip chain, all writing intermediate render targets. I want to keep VRAM usage for these intermediate targets low and stop hand-tracking image barriers and layout transitions between passes. What architecture should I use and what are the correctness pitfalls?
assertions: Recommends a render graph / frame graph where each pass declares its resource reads and writes and the graph derives execution order plus the barriers and image-layout transitions
States that transient targets may share (alias) the same physical memory only when their lifetimes do not overlap
Warns that an aliased target's contents are undefined on first use in its new lifetime, so it must be fully cleared or overwritten before being read

evals.prompt: I want my game to output real HDR to an HDR10 display. Today I render the scene and present to an 8-bit sRGB swapchain. What do I need to change in the swapchain configuration and the final output pass to get correct HDR on the panel?
assertions: Specifies a wide-gamut swapchain: PQ/ST2084 Rec.2020 at 10-bit-or-more per channel (e.g. an A2B10G10R10 packed format) for HDR10, or extended-linear scRGB at FP16 (RGBA16F) — not an 8-bit sRGB backbuffer for the HDR path
Applies the display transfer function exactly once in an explicit final pass and does not rely on an automatic sRGB backbuffer to encode
Scales luminance to the display's actual measured peak nits rather than PQ's full 10,000-nit range

evals.prompt: My explicit-API renderer creates a separate device memory allocation for every texture and buffer. It works in small test scenes but fails once I load a real level with thousands of assets. How should I manage GPU memory instead, and how should I get static texture data onto GPU memory the shaders can sample fast?
assertions: Recommends sub-allocating resources out of a small number of large memory blocks instead of one device allocation per resource, and notes the device allocation count is hard-capped
Uploads static assets by writing to a host-visible staging buffer and copying into a device-local resource, because device-local memory is generally not CPU-mappable
